# Licensing and provenance review

Reviewed 2026-09-24 for the **AVID Core repository**, the source-code library consumed by ATIV and EnCAP. The conclusion applies to the code in this repository and source releases from it. Each consuming application's installer, runtime and code-signing eligibility need their own package audit.

## GPL-3.0-or-later decision

`src/`, `examples/`, and the test code were committed in AVID Core by Tom/Thomas Lothian. The incorporated EnCAP source identified in [docs/provenance.md](docs/provenance.md)—`crates/encap-video/src/lib.rs`, `crates/encap-ffmpeg/src/lib.rs`, and video state in `crates/encap-core/src/model.rs` at [`a96978e`](https://github.com/tlolabs/encap/commit/a96978e5bb89189b944e5dd6a30e5ee7e8fe28d4)—also has only Tom Lothian in its path history. The ATIV-origin inputs at [`2c5eeed`](https://github.com/tlolabs/ativ/commit/2c5eeed27e48d67fed128a62ff74dab6f00c2a82) were already GPL-3.0-or-later. EnCAP itself declares GPL-3.0-only; that earlier nonexclusive grant and prior AVID Core releases remain valid. Thomas, as the identified copyright holder, can grant **this AVID Core version** under GPL-3.0-or-later without relicensing the separate EnCAP repository. The [GNU GPL FAQ](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.en.html#ReleaseUnderGPLAndNF) confirms that a copyright holder can issue different nonexclusive licenses for their own work. No other human author appears in the AVID Core Git history or the histories of those EnCAP source paths. This evidence supports the change requested by the owner; Git metadata alone cannot prove the absence of an unrecorded third-party rights claim.

`Cargo.toml`, the README, and selected original source headers now declare `GPL-3.0-or-later`; `LICENSE` contains the unmodified official GPLv3 text. The declaration covers **AVID Core-owned code**, not independent third-party crates, externally supplied FFmpeg executables, or applications that consume the library. The EnCAP repository's own GPL-3.0-only declaration is unchanged. Copyright notice: Copyright © Thomas Lothian.

The separate `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` is an attributed adaptation of Contributor Covenant 2.1 under its upstream [CC BY 4.0 license](https://github.com/EthicalSource/contributor_covenant/blob/2.1/LICENSE.md); it is not claimed as Thomas's GPL-licensed original code. The [official adoption guide](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/adopt/) invites projects to adapt and publish the text. Its only change here is the reporting-contact instruction.

## Inputs and redistributed material

The published crate is source only. `Cargo.lock` and the [dependency inventory](docs/dependency-inventory.json) record the current resolved packages, checksums and license expressions without relying on a fixed package count. Direct dependencies include `serde`, `serde_json`, `sha2`, `tempfile`, `same-file`, `turbojpeg`, `oxipng`, `zopfli`, `png`, and the exact `turbojpeg-sys`/`libdeflate-sys` native source constraints. The image addition, reviewed 2026-10-19, compiles vendored libjpeg-turbo and libdeflate C source from the pinned Cargo packages into consumers. TurboJPEG's Rust wrappers offer MIT or Unlicense; native libjpeg-turbo's IJG and BSD-3-Clause terms also apply, with Zlib notices retained for optional SIMD source. OxiPNG and native libdeflate use MIT, libdeflater's Rust wrappers and Zopfli use Apache-2.0, and the PNG decoder offers MIT or Apache-2.0. Their original license texts and exact source identities are preserved in [licenses/image-optimization](licenses/image-optimization/README.md), including the required Independent JPEG Group attribution. The inventory records the remaining permissive license alternatives and Unicode terms. [Dependencies](docs/DEPENDENCIES.md) and [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) explain these boundaries and host notice handling. No proprietary Microsoft binary, font or third-party artwork is a runtime component. Small synthetic audio/image fixtures under `tests/fixtures/ffmpeg/` were generated locally from FFmpeg sine and color filters; [their provenance record](tests/fixtures/ffmpeg/provenance.json) gives exact commands and hashes. Other original test inputs are described in [source provenance](docs/provenance.md).

FFmpeg and ffprobe are separate processes, not linked into the Rust crate. Core owns their source-built runtime, dependencies, packaging, provenance, license inventory and verified platform publication under [the provider contract](docs/ffmpeg/provider-contract.md). Hosts select a Core runtime and own application integration, signing and distribution. The crate embeds its pinned runtime specification for authenticated loading; the separate runtime's notices do not replace the image-codec notices required by a linked consumer.

## Windows components and SignPath Foundation

| Exact component or package | AVID Core role and applicable license | GPLv3 System Libraries assessment | Separate SignPath assessment / bundling necessity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `windows-sys/0.61.2`, `windows-link/0.2.1` | Target-specific Rust dependencies in `Cargo.lock`, from Microsoft's [windows-rs](https://github.com/microsoft/windows-rs) project, under `MIT OR Apache-2.0`. They are source dependencies, not proprietary redistributable DLLs. | Their permissive licenses are GPLv3-compatible; no System Libraries exception is needed. | OSI-approved licensing is compatible with SignPath's component rule. They may remain normal Rust dependencies. |
| Windows OS DLLs and Windows API contracts | Windows supplies these to a compiled consumer or test executable under its own [Windows terms](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/Useterms/Retail/Windows/11/UseTerms_Retail_Windows_11_English.htm). AVID Core's source release contains none. Exact imports depend on the host-built binary and cannot be assigned to this source archive. | OS-supplied core libraries fit the GPLv3 [§1 System Libraries definition](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.en.html), as explained in the [GNU FAQ](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.en.html#SystemLibraryException). | SignPath [explicitly permits System Libraries in signed packages](https://signpath.org/terms.html). No OS DLL needs to be bundled in an AVID Core source release. |
| Visual C++ / Universal CRT / MSVC and Windows SDK on CI machines | Windows GitHub-hosted runners and the Rust MSVC target can use these build and test tools; no such binary is tracked or released by AVID Core. The specific preinstalled tool versions vary with the runner image. Microsoft's [VC++ redistributable guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist) applies if a consuming app ships a compiled MSVC executable. | The [GNU Windows runtime FAQ](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.en.html#WindowsRuntimeAndGPL) treats dynamic VC++ runtime linkage as System Library use and cautions against bundling its DLLs with a GPL program under that exception. This is relevant to a host-built binary, not the source crate. | SignPath's explicit System Libraries exception can apply to qualifying runtime components; a future signed binary needs its own exact import and payload inventory. AVID Core need not bundle these files. |
| Windows App SDK, WinUI 3, WebView2, .NET runtime, Windows ML, DirectML | **No AVID Core package reference, link, install, download, or shipped file** for any of these. ATIV's Windows UI is a separate repository and distribution. | There is no AVID Core combined binary involving these components to test for GPL incompatibility or System Library status. Do not infer a conflict from another application's package. | They create no AVID Core source-release SignPath component issue. ATIV must assess its own signed installer or application package, including SignPath's System Libraries exception. |
| Microsoft Sysinternals Handle and other diagnostic tools mentioned in historical documents | Not imported by the library, absent from tracked release binaries, and not downloaded by the current CI workflows. | Build/research-only references do not create a linked GPL combination. | Not an AVID Core signed-package component. |

The [GPLv3 System Libraries exception](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.en.html) and SignPath's identically named but independently administered [policy exception](https://signpath.org/terms.html) answer different questions. Source licensing, a consuming application's combined executable, redistribution of a Microsoft runtime beside that executable, and SignPath Foundation eligibility must be decided separately. No proprietary Microsoft component in this repository prevents licensing AVID Core-owned code GPL-3.0-or-later.

## Release format

AVID Core's Rust library release is a tagged source revision and, if desired, a crates.io source package. It does not require a portable Windows application ZIP, installer, Windows App SDK runtime, or application code signing. Core's separately published FFmpeg runtimes carry their own build and license evidence. Host applications own their application packaging and must include linked image-codec notices. Any SignPath eligibility claim needs an exact inventory of the binary package under assessment.
